headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no shared I/O or write surfaces are documented, but B’s allowlisted egress and A’s data-orchestrator role warrant caution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible injection bridge is documented: dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, browser, or MCP surfaces, and nuwa-skill exposes no shared channel either. Without a channel for A’s outputs to reach B as instructions, the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is provably blocked from the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF B begins parsing A-generated text as instructions, the pathway becomes active.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared copy/paste workflows.
Do not add a shared MCP server without provenance tagging.
Review any future adapter that forwards A’s text into B.
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles show no shared filesystem, no file I/O surfaces, and no touched data classes for either agent. Dagster has no filesystem read/write or network egress, while nuwa-skill only has allowlisted egress; with no documented data flow between them, leakage is not plausible from the current profiles.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced, re-evaluate leakage.
IF either agent is configured to ingest secrets or PHI, the analysis changes.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Confirm nuwa-skill’s allowlist excludes sensitive endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or egress network, and nuwa-skill’s only documented capability is allowlisted egress. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so capability conflict is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk appears.
IF either agent gains OAuth scopes on a shared mutable resource, reassess.
mitigations: Keep dagster read-only in this pairing.
Do not grant shared repo write access.
Document any future shared OAuth scopes.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a data orchestrator and B is a scientific-research agent, so a workflow could pass A’s outputs into B’s reasoning, but the profiles do not show B acting on external side effects or A producing authoritative facts by default. The pathway exists only if an operator wires them together, and the blast radius is limited to incorrect downstream analysis.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A’s outputs as authoritative without verification, cascading error risk increases.
IF A’s outputs are used as inputs to a downstream action-taking system, reassess severity.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to cite independent sources before acting.
Label A outputs as untrusted drafts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A-to-B handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. Dagster is open-source and unverified; nuwa-skill is open-source and verified, but the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or policy mismatches, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned PHI, EU PII, or regulated records, reassess compliance.
IF retention or residency policies are added to one agent but not the other, re-evaluate.
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Review retention settings if added later.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion controls before use with regulated data.
